fields.name: Kṛṣṇakamala Gosvāmī
fields.works: Dramas for the yātrā: Svapna-vilāsa, Nandaharaṇa, Divyonmāda (Rāy-unmādinī), Vicitra-vilāsa, Bhārata-milana, Gāndharvā-milana, Kālīya-damana, Nimāi-sannyāsa
fields.notes: Born 1811 at Bhajanghāṭ (Nadia), of the family of Kaṁsāri Sena, Sadāśiva Kavirāja, Puruṣottama and Kānu Ṭhākura; wrote eight yātrā dramas on Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa and Gaurāṅga līlā, loved by thousands.

Priest of Hiraṇya and Govardhana Majumdār (CC Antya 3.165-166), of Cāndapura; Haridāsa Ṭhākura stayed in his house, where young Raghunātha dāsa visited him daily; he brought Haridāsa to the Majumdārs' court, where Gopāla Cakravartī (#1935) insulted him.

fields.name: Halāyudha
fields.notes: Ninth from Dakṣa Maharṣi (one of Ādiśūra's five brāhmaṇas from Kānyakubja); minister of Rājā Lakṣmaṇa Sena; wrote many books. Saved by Śrī Dāmodara Śālagrāma when he tried to burn himself to atone for a sin of his youth.

fields.name: Kṛṣṇadayāla Candra (Pāñcthupi)
fields.appearance: Early in the 17th Śaka century (the record's text)
fields.disciples: Advaita dāsa Bābājī of Vṛndāvana (#17, kīrtana); his company woke Banwārīlāl Siṁha (#93)
fields.notes: A Suvarṇa-vaṇik of Pāñcthupi, devout Vaiṣṇava and Manoharaśāhī kīrtana singer (taught by Kṛṣṇahari Hājrā); studied grammar and the Bhāgavatam under Rāmakṛṣṇa Vidyābhūṣaṇa of Muniādihi; friend of Rāmasundara Tarkavāgīśa. Teacher of Advaita dāsa Bābājī; surely the Kṛṣṇadayāla who woke renunciation in Banwārīlāl Siṁha of Pāñcthupi.

fields.name: Ānandī
fields.works: Ṭīkā on Prabodhānanda's Śrī Caitanya-candrāmṛta (1723); Śīghrabodha (grammar, 1718)

fields.name: Hemādri
fields.works: Caturvarga-cintāmaṇi; Āyurveda-rasāyana; Cintāmaṇi; Kāmadhenu; Kalpadruma; Rāja-praśasti
fields.notes: Minister of the Yādava kings of Devagiri (1260-1309); took shelter of Vopadeva; compiled the Caturvarga-cintāmaṇi on Smṛti and other works.

fields.guru: Harinātha, son of Dāmodara dāsa (brother of Gopīnātha Pūjārī)
fields.works: Bhāvabhāva-vibhāvikā (on the Rāsa-pañcādhyāya); Prabhu (on the Śrī Gaurāṅga-candrodaya); Sūkṣmatama-vṛtti (on the Brahma-sūtra)
fields.notes: Disciple of Harinātha, of the family of Gopīnātha Pūjārī of Śrī Rādhāramaṇa (Gopāla Bhaṭṭa's line); wrote the Bhāvabhāva-vibhāvikā, the Prabhu commentary and a Sūkṣmatama-vṛtti on the Brahma-sūtra, the last in places out of tune with Mahāprabhu's tradition.

fields.name: Vāsudeva Śiyāla
fields.notes: A brāhmaṇa of Rāḍha, first a Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava, expelled for misconduct (Prema-vilāsa 24); one of the impostors who posed as incarnations when Mahāprabhu's worship spread (with Viṣṇudāsa Kapīndra, Mādhava Cūḍādhārī); «Śiyāla» = jackal.

fields.name: Gopīramaṇa Cakravartī
fields.guru: Hṛdayānanda (Bhakti-ratnākara 14.97); Govardhana dāsa Dāmodara (Rasikamaṅgala); Narottama Ṭhākura (Narottama-vilāsa, Prema-vilāsa)
fields.notes: Named in three sources as disciple of Hṛdayānanda (at the installation of Rādhāvinoda), of Govardhana dāsa Dāmodara (śrīpāṭa at Budhurī) and of Narottama (in charge of lodgings at Kheturī); perhaps two or three persons.

Eldest son of Rasikānanda Prabhu (Rasikamaṅgala Paścima 14.27, 31-33), born 1615; head of Śyāmānanda's gaddī at Gopīvallabhapura at fourteen; scholar and musician; wrote the Śrī Rādhā-Govinda Kāvya after the Gīta-govinda. Died 1684; sons Nayanānanda (#2006) and Rasānanda.

Daughter of Mahārāja Pratāparudra, married to Kṛṣṇadeva Rāya of Vijayanagara (#775) with the seized lands as dowry; ill-treated, she left him and lived quietly at Kambam; composed the Tukkā-pañcakam (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).
